text: Imagine you are walking down a crowded metropolitan street on a chaotic Monday morning.
Car horns blare incessantly, sirens scream in the distance, and hundreds of hurried commuters brush past your shoulders.
Suddenly, your fingers brush against an intricate golden pocket watch hidden inside your coat.
You pull it out, inspect its polished brass gears, and press down firmly on the crown.
A flock of pigeons halts mid-flap in mid-air, suspended as if pinned by invisible needles.
A spilled cup of hot cappuccino hangs tilted in empty space, droplets of espresso frozen like molten amber beads.
A speeding yellow taxi skids to an absolute halt, its front bumper resting barely an inch away from a terrified pedestrian whose expression is locked in place.
At this moment, a rush of pure euphoria surges through your veins.
You feel like an omnipotent god.
You imagine walking into luxury boutiques, rearranging people's luggage, exploring secret rooms, or casually wandering into a maximum-security bank vault without a single soul ever noticing.
In almost every Hollywood blockbuster and comic book saga, pausing time is celebrated as the most convenient, elegant, and invincible superpower in the universe.
Because the very second you press that button, the cold, unyielding laws of fundamental physics will transform your childhood fantasy into an inescapable cosmic nightmare.
